question: The head chef, along with his three junior assistants, cooks delicious meals, but the main courses cooks too slowly during peak hours. Identify the incorrect part.

options.A: The head chef, along with his three junior assistants
options.C: but the main courses cooks too slowly

solution.incorrectPart: the main courses cooks too slowly
solution.correctPart: the main courses cook too slowly
explanation: Rule 1: The phrase 'along with' does not change the number of the main subject.
Rule 2: The subject 'main courses' is plural and requires a plural verb.
Application: Use 'cook' instead of 'cooks' with the plural subject.
Correct sentence: The head chef, along with his three junior assistants, cooks delicious meals, but the main courses cook too slowly during peak hours.

question: Not only the principal but also the senior teachers was invited to address the school assembly this morning. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: to address the school assembly this morning

explanation: Rule 1: With 'not only...but also', the verb generally agrees with the subject closest to it.
Rule 2: The nearest subject is 'senior teachers', which is plural.
Application: Use 'were invited' to agree with the plural subject.
Correct sentence: Not only the principal but also the senior teachers were invited to address the school assembly this morning.

question: Each of the newly elected student council representatives were awarded a certificate of merit by the chief guest. Identify the incorrect part.

options.A: Each of the newly elected student council representatives

explanation: Rule 1: 'Each of + plural noun' takes a singular verb in formal subject-verb agreement.
Rule 2: The main subject is 'each', not 'representatives'.
Application: Use 'was awarded' because 'each' is singular.
Correct sentence: Each of the newly elected student council representatives was awarded a certificate of merit by the chief guest.

question: Neither of the two proposed solutions seem practical under the current financial constraints of the project. Identify the incorrect part.

options.A: Neither of the two proposed solutions

explanation: Rule 1: 'Neither' used as a pronoun takes a singular verb in formal English.
Rule 2: The phrase 'of the two proposed solutions' does not change the subject's number.
Application: Use 'seems' with the singular subject 'neither'.
Correct sentence: Neither of the two proposed solutions seems practical under the current financial constraints of the project.

question: Either of the two master chefs cook the special curry when the restaurant gets busy, and both cooks well. Identify the parts containing errors.

options.A: Either of the two master chefs cook
options.B: the special curry when the restaurant gets busy

explanation: Rule 1: 'Either of + plural noun' takes a singular verb in formal English.
Rule 2: 'Either of the two master chefs' requires 'cooks'.
Rule 3: The pronoun 'both' is plural and requires the verb 'cook'.
Application: Correct both verbs: 'cook' becomes 'cooks', and 'cooks' becomes 'cook'.
Correct sentence: Either of the two master chefs cooks the special curry when the restaurant gets busy, and both cook well.

question: Everybody in the classroom were eager to participate in the interactive science demonstration. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: to participate in the interactive science demonstration

explanation: Rule 1: Indefinite pronouns such as 'everybody', 'everyone', and 'nobody' are grammatically singular.
Rule 2: The subject 'everybody' takes a singular verb.
Application: Use 'was eager' instead of 'were eager'.
Correct sentence: Everybody in the classroom was eager to participate in the interactive science demonstration.

question: A lot of effort were put into organizing the cultural fest by the student volunteers. Identify the incorrect part.

explanation: Rule 1: With 'a lot of', the verb agrees with the noun following 'of'.
Rule 2: 'Effort' is an uncountable noun used here in the singular sense.
Application: Use 'was put' to agree with 'effort'.
Correct sentence: A lot of effort was put into organizing the cultural fest by the student volunteers.

question: There is a few milk left in the refrigerator, so we do not need to buy any more today. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: so we do not need to buy any more today

explanation: Rule 1: 'A few' is used with plural countable nouns.
Rule 2: 'Milk' is an uncountable noun.
Application: Use 'a little' with uncountable nouns.
Correct sentence: There is a little milk left in the refrigerator, so we do not need to buy any more today.

question: The rich is expected to contribute generously to the local community relief fund during times of crisis. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: to the local community relief fund during times of crisis

explanation: Rule 1: 'The + adjective' can refer to a whole class of people.
Rule 2: 'The rich' refers to rich people collectively and takes a plural verb.
Application: Use 'are expected' instead of 'is expected'.
Correct sentence: The rich are expected to contribute generously to the local community relief fund during times of crisis.

question: Rahul is one of those talented musicians who plays the violin exceptionally well in the school orchestra. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: the violin exceptionally well in the school orchestra

explanation: Rule 1: In 'one of those + plural noun + who', the relative pronoun 'who' generally refers to the plural noun.
Rule 2: Here, 'who' refers to 'musicians', which is plural.
Application: Use 'play' to agree with the plural antecedent 'musicians'.
Correct sentence: Rahul is one of those talented musicians who play the violin exceptionally well in the school orchestra.
